name: Question 14
problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)={e}^{-t}p(t)$ at the point where $t=0$, if $p(0)=\,i+\,j+k$ and ${p}^{′}(0)=\,i-\,j.$
worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}.
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})p(t)+{e}^{-t}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-{e}^{-t}p(t)+{e}^{-t}{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =-{e}^{0}p(0)+{e}^{0}{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =-(\,i+\,j+k)+(\,i-\,j) \\  & =-2j-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(-2j-k) \\  & =-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}j-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is $T(0)=-\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}j-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}k.$

Question 14

Find the unit tangent vector to the curve r(t)=e−tp(t) at the point where t=0, if p(0)=i+j+k and p′(0)=i−j.

a
−255i−55k
b
−255i−55k
c
−255j−55k
d
−255j+55k
e
−255j−55k
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a curve r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k, the unit tangent vector T(t) at the point P(x(t),y(t),z(t)) is given by T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖.

First, we find r′(t) and evaluate it at t=0:

r′(t)=ddt(e−tp(t))=ddt(e−t)p(t)+e−tddt(p(t))=−e−tp(t)+e−tp′(t)r′(0)=−e0p(0)+e0p′(0)=−(i+j+k)+(i−j)=−2j−k

Now, we calculate the magnitude of r′(0):

‖r′(0)‖=(0)2+(−2)2+(1)2=0+4+1=5

Finally, we normalize r′(0):

T(0)=r′(0)‖r′(0)‖=15(−2j−k)=−255j−55k

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to t=0 is T(0)=−255j−55k.
